title: application errors
description: Application error shape and code catalog. Application codes live outside the JSON-RPC reserved range (-32768..-32000), grouped by domain: 1xxx daemon, 2xxx ACP session, 3xxx propose, 4xxx worktree orchestration. Contract messages are in English; the remedy field lets surfaces translate or expand.

kind.description: Machine-readable error kind, stable across daemon versions.

detail.description: Human-readable English detail of what went wrong.

remedy.description: Actionable English suggestion for how to fix it.

candidates.description: The fleet agents detected on this system, carried by a refusal to resolve one (2000/2001) so a surface can offer a choice instead of transcribing a lament. Absent means the error has nothing to do with resolving an agent; an empty array means the fleet was consulted and nothing was found — which is an answer, not an omission.

leverRefused.description: The lever a session refused when it opened, when the error is that refusal (2007): the same record its log keeps, so a surface can say it in its own words.

leverRefusal.description: A lever refused when its session opened, before any prompt: what the session log records and what the 2007 error carries. Lists are bounded and say how many were left out.

reason.description: not_announced: no option of the lever's category; ambiguous: more than one; not_a_value: the value is not among the announced ones, or a toggle got neither true nor false; not_confirmed: the agent's answer left another value, or none; mode_changed: setting the lever changed the agent's mode; no_answer: no answer within the wait.

values.description: The values the agent announced for the lever's option.

options.description: The options the agent announced, when none or several carried the lever's category.

more.description: How many values or options were left out of those lists.

left.description: What the agent left instead: the value its answer kept, or the mode it moved to.

agentCandidate.description: One agent offered as a way out of a resolution refusal, in the vocabulary fleet/list publishes and computed by the same detection path, so the error and the Fleet view cannot disagree. Ids, detection, state and remedies only: never an environment value, a credential path or anything shaped like a secret (fair play §2).

id.description: Stable catalog identifier, the same one agent.id selects.

detected.description: Whether this agent's pilot point was found on this system.

installState.description: The composed install state across the entry's layers, identical to the one fleet/list reports for it.

remedy.description: Which layer is missing and what to do about it, in one sentence.

remedyCommand.description: The exact command that installs the missing layer. Data, never run.

errorObject.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 error object with structured data.

1000.description: The client declared a proto/ contract version the daemon does not support. detail carries both the requested and the supported versions; the connection is closed after the response.

1001.description: A method other than initialize was called before a successful initialize on this connection.

1002.description: The daemon is shutting down and no longer accepts work.

2000.description: Neither agent.command nor agent.id is configured. remedy points to the user or project config file, and data.candidates carries the agents detected on this system so a surface can offer a choice rather than transcribe the sentence.

2001.description: The selected agent is not present on this system: the configured catalog id is unknown, or its binary was not detected. detail names the missing id or command; remedy explains how to configure or install it, and data.candidates carries the detected agents with their install state. Nothing is launched and nothing degrades to another provider.

2002.description: The agent subprocess could not be started.

2003.description: The ACP initialize negotiation with the agent failed. On version incompatibility, detail carries both protocol versions; the subprocess is terminated.

2004.description: The given sessionId does not correspond to an active session.

2005.description: A subscription link or unlink was refused: the catalog entry declares no auth-context variable, the name is invalid or already linked, or the profile lives in hand-written configuration. The detail says which and the remedy says what to do instead.

2006.description: A per-session lever the resolved agent does not accept — a model or an effort level its provider has no documented place for. Refused rather than ignored: a quota lever that silently does nothing is worse than no lever, because the user believes they lowered their spend. The detail names the agent and the lever.

2007.description: A configuration the agent never announced or never confirmed. Live, from session/set-config-option: an unknown option id, a value the option does not list, or a session whose agent announced no options at all. At open, from every verb that starts an agent: a model or effort that goes by the agent's announcement and has no single option of its category, is not among the announced values, is not confirmed by the agent's answer, moves the agent's mode, or gets no answer in time — the session ends as lever_refused with no prompt sent, data.kind is lever_refused and data.leverRefused carries the lever, what was asked, the reason and what the agent announced or left, bounded. Distinct from 2006, which is refused before the session exists against what the agent's entry declares; this one is refused against what THIS agent said about THIS session. It is what keeps Meltemi from offering a selector on the agent's behalf, or prompting a model nobody chose.

3000.description: The derived change name already exists under .meltemi/changes/. detail includes the conflicting name; remedy suggests an available alternative. Nothing is modified.

3001.description: No change name can be derived from the given idea.

3002.description: projectRoot does not exist or is not a directory.

4000.description: Worktree orchestration was requested on a directory that is not a git repository. detail states the directory is not a git repo; remedy points to `git init` (or opening an existing repo). Simple sessions still work, without isolation, warned.

4001.description: A managed-worktree or checkpoint operation was refused: the target is not one the daemon created, it has uncommitted changes, or the required confirmation was not given. Foreign worktrees are never touched; dirty removals and reversions need explicit confirmation.

4002.description: No checkpoint exists for the requested change/task/agent. detail names the missing task; remedy suggests listing checkpoints. Nothing is reverted.

4003.description: The per-task commit could not be created — most often a user git hook rejected it. detail carries the git/hook output verbatim; hooks are never bypassed (no --no-verify). The task stays completed-without-commit, a visible state.

4004.description: Archiving was blocked: a requirement is neither verified (linked to a test or manually marked) nor excepted with a justification. detail lists the unverified scenarios; nothing is folded into the living truth.

4005.description: Archiving was blocked: applying the change's deltas to the living truth raised conflict diagnostics (e.g. a modified requirement that does not exist). detail lists them; nothing is folded — the living truth is left intact.

4006.description: A change/show, spec/show or sdd/validate named a change or capability that does not exist under .meltemi/. detail names it; remedy points at change/list or spec/list. Nothing is read further.

5000.description: An analytics/usage query is unusable as written (inverted range, unparseable bound, empty limit). detail says which parameter and remedy how to write it; the daemon never substitutes a default period in silence.

6000.description: Identity could not be answered: no [identity] table in the user's configuration, no mesh client where it was named, or a client that is present and not signed in. detail names which of the three and remedy says what to do; a status answer with available:false carries the same reason without being an error.
